subdomain: 4.2 Design evaluation datasets and test frameworks using mixed methodologies

en.question: A data-migration benchmark requires an approval before any write, correct final records, and a verified row count. A candidate meets all three using an allowed bulk-update API, but the grader fails it for not using the reference solution's row-by-row tool sequence. How should the test framework change?

options.text: Check approval ordering and final-state invariants while allowing valid update strategies.
options.note: Approval ordering is a real intermediate business requirement and must remain enforced. The particular update sequence is not required, so the grader should accept any permitted strategy that produces the verified outcome.

options.text: Require the row-by-row sequence in the agent prompt to align with the reference.
options.note: This makes the implementation imitate an unnecessarily rigid grader. It excludes an allowed bulk strategy without improving compliance with the actual migration requirements.

options.text: Grade only final record equality and remove all intermediate-action checks.
options.note: Final-state equality alone would miss writes performed before approval. Intermediate checks are justified when, as here, their ordering is itself a stated safety or business requirement.

options.text: Accept every trial that invokes the bulk-update API without an exception.
options.note: An exception-free call does not prove correct records, verified counts, or approval before writing. Replacing one sequence proxy with another would still fail to grade the full contract.

references.title: Anthropic Engineering: Demystifying evals for AI agents
